videos.script: Ipê keeps every prescription it has ever received. Twenty-nine thousand of them, the oldest from 2019. Nobody decided to keep them forever. Nobody decided anything. {{forever}} This lesson writes the decision down. A table that says how long each kind of record stays, from which day, and why. Counted from the wrong day, a rule like that breaks a different law. {{schedule}} Then a purge that obeys it: nine thousand prescriptions, nine hundred orders, three hundred tickets, gone in one run. Except one customer's, because that customer is in court, and the hold says so. {{purge}} Before the orders go, what they say about sales is kept as totals that name nobody. {{totals}} And a trail of who changed what, which refuses to be changed itself, including by the one statement people forget. {{trail}} Data that was deleted cannot leak. Deleting it on purpose, on time, and provably, is the part of governance most companies never get to. {{end}}
